issue.title: test_candidates_fast_path_wall_clock_budget[patch] and [monitor] fail under the full parallel lane: a wall-clock assertion cannot hold under contention
issue.description:
FOUND BY the sase-p8 land agent (2026-08-18) during the epic's landing verification run. Unrelated to that epic's diff (a CLI hand-off command; no completion code touched).

REPRODUCTION: tests/main/test_completion_candidates_contract.py::test_candidates_fast_path_wall_clock_budget[patch] and [monitor] both failed under a full parallel run of 32,922 tests on master c033ca4c4 ('10 failed, 32912 passed, 12 skipped in 601s'), and both passed when rerun in isolation with -p no:randomly, where the same parametrizations complete in about 0.13s each.

WHY IT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT INCIDENTAL: this test asserts a WALL-CLOCK budget for the completion fast path. Wall clock on a box running an xdist lane at full width measures scheduler contention, not the code under test — the budget can be blown by any other worker, so the node is guaranteed to be intermittently red at some load, on some host, forever. The other two parametrizations that ran in the same suite ([model], [bead], [workspace], [plan], [repo]) were unaffected in this run, which is itself evidence of load-luck rather than a per-parametrization defect.

SCOPE, IN PREFERENCE ORDER:
1. Replace the wall-clock bound with a deterministic proxy for what the budget is really protecting — a call/IO count, or process CPU time (time.process_time) instead of time.perf_counter — so the assertion measures the fast path rather than the host.
2. If a wall-clock bound must stay, mark the node serial (or exclude it from the parallel lane) so it is measured under known conditions, and state the assumed load in the failure message.
3. Widening the budget is the weakest option: it does not remove the dependence on host load, it only moves the threshold.

NO EXISTING BEAD: 'sase bead search' over task beads for 'wall_clock_budget|fast_path_wall_clock' returns nothing, so this node is not yet tracked.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-j7 — in-progress epic 'Fix the sase-ct flake class at its root'. That epic targets process-global state leaking between tests; this node's mechanism is different (a wall-clock budget measuring host contention), so it likely needs its own fix rather than being subsumed.

evidence.note:
Third parametrization of the same node, independently observed by the sase-p4 land agent (2026-08-18, clean master 66b884434). 'just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake' lists

  tests/main/test_completion_candidates_contract.py::test_candidates_fast_path_wall_clock_budget[agent]

among the 5 nodes exceeding tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt, while [patch] and [monitor] (this bead's originals) do not currently exceed it. The node passes at HEAD in a full 33,003-test run. That a third, different parametrization is the one over the line this week is direct support for this bead's 'load-luck rather than a per-parametrization defect' analysis and for scope option 1 (replace the wall-clock bound with a deterministic proxy) over option 3 (widen the budget), since widening would just move which parametrization loses the contention lottery.

Originally surfaced as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on closed phase bead sase-p4.3 (2026-08-18T02:58Z), which recorded [agent] as one of 3 then-unfiled completion nodes; the other two are corroborated on sase-o0.

Fourth parametrization of the same node observed: tests/main/test_completion_candidates_contract.py::test_candidates_fast_path_wall_clock_budget[agent] failed under just check-full's full parallel lane in workspace sase_13 (2026-08-18, monitor zekexy4knqvt run). Same wall-clock-under-contention mechanism; unrelated to the agent-role phase-label rename being landed.
